question:
In the given figure, ABCD and APQR are two parallelograms. If ∠APQ = 100°, find ∠CDR. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ea4fa9986e7e2ac3bd6759ddc11b0dd98cb3f211e3e93355f74c2ad839f625fc.png]
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

In a parallelogram, adjacent angles are supplementary (sum = 180°).

In parallelogram APQR, ∠A + ∠P = 180° ⇒ ∠A = 180° − 100° = 80°.

In parallelogram ABCD, opposite angles are equal.

∠C = ∠A = 80°.

**∴ The correct answer is 80°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** ABCD and APQR are parallelograms sharing vertex A. ∠APQ = 100°.

**Formula:** 1. Adjacent angles of a parallelogram sum to 180°. 2. Opposite angles of a parallelogram are equal.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d44b9eee8d70a7f5a2c92dba32482958a4284bd87a797f0fea4c8aaa702de1f0.png] 

In parallelogram APQR:

⇒ ∠PAR + ∠APQ = 180° (Consecutive interior angles)

⇒ ∠PAR + 100° = 180°

⇒ ∠PAR = 80°

Since A, P, B and A, R, D are collinear, ∠DAB = ∠PAR = 80°.

In parallelogram ABCD:

⇒ ∠BCD = ∠DAB (Opposite angles are equal)

⇒ ∠BCD = 80°

**∴ The correct answer is 80°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Properties of a Parallelogram

Opposite sides are equal and parallel. Opposite angles are equal, and any two consecutive angles are supplementary (∠A + ∠B = 180°).

Diagonals of a Parallelogram

The diagonals of a parallelogram bisect each other, meaning they divide each other into two equal parts at the point of intersection.

Area of a Parallelogram

The area is calculated as Base × Height. If two sides a, b and the included angle θ are known, Area = a × b × sin(θ).</p
